Kalynivske Jewish Сemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kherson Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Kalynivske was founded in 1807 as the Jewish agricultural colony of Seydemenukha by settlers from the Vitebsk, Mogilev, and Chernigov Governorates, later becoming known as Bolshaya (Great) Seydemenukha after a daughter colony split off nearby in 1841 — documented elsewhere in this collection. In 1926, the colony's own Jews founded a further daughter colony, Roytfeld. In 1927 it was renamed Kalinindorf and became the center of the Kalinindorf Jewish National Raion, an administrative district encompassing 11 village councils, 8 of them Jewish, with its own Yiddish-language school, agricultural school, teacher-training college, and newspaper — a genuinely complete infrastructure for Soviet Yiddish cultural autonomy. Most of the colony's remaining Jews were murdered in September 1941.
